title: By one year, most babies look for a toy they watched you place
summary: The CDC says that by one year, most babies look for things they see you place, like a toy under a blanket.
body: On the milestones-by-one-year page, the CDC's cognitive list says a baby looks for things he sees you place, like a toy under a blanket. The item is a search after a placement the baby watched. It is what the page says most babies do by a first birthday. It is the US checklist, not a pass-fail exam for one baby. The child watched the placement under the cover. The line is a checklist item for a first birthday.

sources.title: Milestones by 1 Year
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the cognitive item about looking for things the baby sees you hide, like a toy under a blanket.
